name: Microsoft Office desktop apps
tagline: The desktop Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook suite, sold as part of Microsoft 365.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: You can absolutely one-shot an editor. You cannot one-shot Excel's calculation engine, forty years of .docx and .xlsx edge cases, or the fact that the accountant, the client and the government form all expect a real Office file back. The parts that look easy, typing text into a box, are the parts nobody pays for; the parts people pay for are pivot tables that match to the cent, tracked changes that survive a round trip through someone else's Word, and a PowerPoint that renders identically on a projector you have never seen. Open source alternatives already exist and are more mature than anything an agent writes in a session, and even they get compatibility complaints. If your actual use is notes and simple tables, skip the suite entirely; if it is interop with other humans, pay.
coreLoopDIY: A local desktop workspace with a Markdown document editor and a formula-capable spreadsheet grid that can import and export .docx and .xlsx well enough for simple files.
requirements: Node 20+ and a desktop shell (Tauri or Electron)
Open source libraries for the file formats: SheetJS, docx, mammoth
Acceptance that anything beyond simple formatting will round-trip badly
whatYouLose: Fidelity: complex .docx and .xlsx files will lose formatting, comments, tracked changes and charts on the way through
Excel's calc engine: hundreds of functions, array formulas, pivot tables, Power Query, and numeric behaviour other people's models depend on
PowerPoint entirely, including rendering that matches on someone else's machine
Outlook, Exchange calendars, and the corporate identity plumbing around them
The included cloud storage, mobile and web apps, and coauthoring that comes bundled with the subscription
moatNotes: The file formats are technically documented and practically bottomless. Everyone else's expectations are the real lock-in.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because documents are social objects. Nobody buys Word to write, they buy it so the file they send opens correctly on the other side, so the spreadsheet the finance team maintains keeps calculating the same numbers, and so the deck does not reflow on the conference room screen. Add decades of trained muscle memory, templates, macros and institutional forms that assume Office, plus a bundle that quietly includes cloud storage and mobile apps, and the subscription is cheaper than the coordination cost of leaving. The people who genuinely can leave usually already did, to LibreOffice or Google Docs, not to something they built.
notes: An editor is a weekend; a document format is not. The moat is every other person who will open your file and expect it to look right.
prompt:
Build a local desktop "personal documents workspace" as an honest consolation prize for Microsoft Office. Do not attempt to clone Office.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Tauri 2 with a React 18 + TypeScript + Vite frontend.
- Local filesystem only. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics.
- SQLite via tauri-plugin-sql only for the recent-files list and window state.

Two modules, both operating on files the user picks from disk:

1. Documents
- A Markdown editor using CodeMirror 6 with a live preview pane.
- Import .docx by converting to Markdown with mammoth. Warn clearly in the UI that formatting, comments and tracked changes are lost.
- Export to .docx using the docx library, and to PDF by printing the preview.
- Native format is plain .md on disk. No proprietary container.

2. Spreadsheets
- A grid using react-data-grid.
- Formulas evaluated with HyperFormula. Support the functions HyperFormula gives you and nothing more.
- Import and export .xlsx with SheetJS (values and formulas only, no charts, no pivot tables, no conditional formatting).
- Native format is .csv plus a sidecar .json holding formulas and column widths.

Shared requirements:
- Tabbed interface, unsaved-change indicators, Cmd/Ctrl+S saves in place.
- On every import, show a non-dismissible fidelity notice listing exactly what was dropped.
- Full-text search across the recent-files list.

Explicitly out of scope: presentations, email, calendars, real-time collaboration, tracked changes, macros, pivot tables, charts.

Deliver a README that states plainly that this handles simple documents and simple spreadsheets, that anything needing to survive a round trip with a real Office user should stay in Office or LibreOffice, and how to run it in dev and build a release binary. Put any keys or paths in .env, though this build should need none.
